newsitem.title: USA: Emergency call made before Colorado murder -report.
newsitem.headline: Emergency call made before Colorado murder -report.

text.p: Three days before six-year-old JenBenet Ramsey was found strangled in her Boulder, Colorado home, police received an emergency phone call from the house, a local newspaper reported on Thursday.

But The Denver Post, which saw police dispatch records, said whoever dialed the 911 number hung up immediately and it was not known if the call had any connection to the murder of the young beauty pageant winner.

Boulder police spokesman Kelvin McNeill said the department had no comment on the 911 call. He also said no arrangements have been made for police to formally interview the parents, John and Patricia Ramsey.

The police spoke to the parents on Dec. 26, the same day they were called to the home after the mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000. Eight hours later, John Ramsey found the child's body in a windowless basement room.

Police also spoke to the parents when they collected blood, hair and handwriting samples from them, McNeill said. But police have been unable to persuade the Ramseys to talk to them formally. "In this country the police cannot force you to talk," McNeill noted.
The Ramseys -- he is a prominent business executive and his wife a former Miss West Virginia -- have hired separate attorneys and a public relations expert from Washington D.C.

Boulder Police Chief Tom Koby, who has kept a tight lid on the progress of the investigation, was due to meet publicly with Boulder residents on Thursday evening, but he was not expected to disclose any significant elements of the probe.
Police have said they are keeping quiet on many aspects of their search for the murderer or murderers in order to protect the integrity of the investigation.
